disease_label_per_paper: Severe community-onset healthcare-associated Clostridium difficile infection complicated by toxic megacolon, septic shock, and KPC-Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream infection
presentation_summary: 63-year-old man with hypertension, multi-infarct dementia, Parkinson disease, and depression had recent hospitalization for E. coli urinary tract infection treated with intravenous ciprofloxacin and oral cefditoren.
He was readmitted with confusion, fever, and diarrhea; C. difficile testing was performed and high-dose oral vancomycin, IV metronidazole, and piperacillin-tazobactam were started.
After 72 hours of deterioration he was transferred to ICU unconscious with GCS 3, ileus, and septic shock syndrome.
At ICU admission he required orotracheal intubation, fluid resuscitation, norepinephrine, and tigecycline; labs showed WBC 24, creatinine 3.6 mg/dL, albumin 2.2 g/dL, and lactate 4 mmol/L.

CT showed toxic megacolon; total colectomy was performed, but he died 24 hours after surgery. Blood cultures grew carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae and one culture grew vancomycin-susceptible Enterococcus faecium.
